leaves.doc: A family *DS-shatters* a set when its traces there contain a pseudo-cube.
leaves.pretty: {X : Type u_1} → {Y : Type u_2} → Set (X → Y) → Set X → Prop

leaves.doc:
A family has *DS dimension* at most `d` when every set it DS-shatters has size at most
`d`.
leaves.pretty: {X : Type u_1} → {Y : Type u_2} → ℕ → Set (X → Y) → Prop

leaves.doc:
A family has *Natarajan dimension* at most `d` when every pair pattern it pair-shatters has
support of size at most `d`.
leaves.pretty: {X : Type u_1} → {Y : Type u_2} → ℕ → Set (X → Y) → Prop

leaves.doc:
A pattern is a *pair pattern* when it offers either no constraint or exactly two labels at
each point. The two labels are recorded as a set, so their order carries no information.
leaves.pretty: {X : Type u_1} → {Y : Type u_2} → (X → Set Y) → Prop

leaves.doc:
A family of labellings of `S` is a *pseudo-cube* when it is nonempty and finite and every
member has, in every direction, a neighbour in the family differing there and agreeing
everywhere else. Over two labels the pseudo-cubes are exactly the Boolean cubes; over more
labels there are others.
leaves.pretty: {X : Type u_1} → {Y : Type u_2} → {S : Set X} → Set (↑S → Y) → Prop

leaves.doc:
A family *pair-shatters* a pattern when every choice of one admissible label per constrained
point is realised by some member.
leaves.pretty: {X : Type u_1} → {Y : Type u_2} → Set (X → Y) → (X → Set Y) → Prop

leaves.doc: The points at which a pattern constrains a concept.
leaves.pretty: {X : Type u_1} → {Y : Type u_2} → (X → Set Y) → Set X

leaves.doc:
The six-cycle read as a family of labellings of a two-point domain. Its traces form a
two-dimensional pseudo-cube containing no two-dimensional Boolean cube, a six-cycle having no
four-cycle.
The edges of a six-cycle on six labels.

nodes.doc:
**`HasDSDimLE.hasNatarajanDimLE` has no converse.** The six-cycle on a two-point domain has
Natarajan dimension `1`, a Natarajan witness on both points being a four-cycle, while its whole
trace family is a two-dimensional pseudo-cube, so its DS dimension is at least `2`.

This is the hexagon Brukhim, Carmon, Dinur, Moran and Yehudayoff record after their Definition 6,
and the four-cycle test the proof turns on is their Example 7. Their Theorem 2 pushes the
separation to a class of Natarajan dimension `1` and infinite DS dimension; that construction
rests on hyperbolic pseudo-manifolds and is cited in the module docstring rather than formalised
here.

nodes.pretty:
∀ {P : Fin 2 → Set (Fin 6)},
  PairShatters sixCycle✝ P →
    pairSupport P = Set.univ → ∀ {y₀ y₁ : Fin 6}, y₀ ∈ P 0 → y₁ ∈ P 1 → sixCycleEdge✝ y₀ y₁ = true

∀ (a b c d : Fin 6),
  sixCycleEdge✝ a c = true →
    sixCycleEdge✝ a d = true → sixCycleEdge✝ b c = true → sixCycleEdge✝ b d = true → a = b ∨ c = d

∀ (c : Fin 2 → Fin 6),
  sixCycleEdge✝ (c 0) (c 1) = true →
    ∀ (i : Fin 2), ∃ c', sixCycleEdge✝ (c' 0) (c' 1) = true ∧ c' i ≠ c i ∧ ∀ (j : Fin 2), j ≠ i → c' j = c j

nodes.doc:
A family whose members each have, in every direction, a neighbour in the family is
DS-shattered on the whole domain.

hypotheses.name: hnbr
hypotheses.pretty: ∀ c ∈ 𝒞, ∀ (i : X), ∃ c' ∈ 𝒞, c' i ≠ c i ∧ ∀ (j : X), j ≠ i → c' j = c j

nodes.pretty:
∀ {X : Type u_1} {Y : Type u_2} {𝒞 : Set (X → Y)},
  𝒞.Nonempty →
    (Set.univ.restrict '' 𝒞).Finite →
      (∀ c ∈ 𝒞, ∀ (i : X), ∃ c' ∈ 𝒞, c' i ≠ c i ∧ ∀ (j : X), j ≠ i → c' j = c j) → DSShatters 𝒞 Set.univ
